answer.summary: “Novelty search” means gradually bringing in people with varied perspectives so the group explores a wider range of ideas. Alex says this should happen carefully, while preserving the group’s norms; in a low-stakes, bottom-up community, ideas that others choose to build on can emerge into useful insights.

sections.heading: Meaning of novelty search
sections.content: Alex uses “novelty search” for seeking out and adding people with different perspectives, thereby searching across the range of perspectives represented in the group—not steering everyone toward one predetermined idea. He recommends adding new perspectives incrementally (about every one to three weeks), because adding too many at once can scramble the norms; he also warns that one person can disrupt the group.

sections.heading: Why it matters in an idea community
sections.content: In the low-stakes, emergent environment Alex describes, people choose what interests them and may build on ideas they find surprising and potentially valuable. If multiple people build on the same idea, he sees that as a good sign it is interesting. The community can then spin off insights organically, but Alex cautions that it cannot be forced toward a particular outcome.
